Subject: On-prem K8s blueprint: IO surface separation & node credentialing onboarding

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for the run-through on Tuesday. As we prepare the on-prem deployment blueprint for Nephro, I wanted to align on two cross-cutting items that impact cluster sizing and ops:

1) IO surface separation — we recommend isolating ephemeral GPU/worker disk IO from persistent model stores and logs. For your workloads (seq length spikes + large KV caches) we suggest:
   - Dedicated NVMe for inference worker local scratch (node-local)
   - Network-attached block store (iSCSI/CSI) for model artifacts with provisioner that supports async detach
   - Separate network interface for storage traffic (VLAN or SR-IOV) with egress policing

2) Node credentialing & onboarding — since your site needs operator-level access control and air-gapped updates, we propose a credentialing playbook: short-lived bootstrap tokens + hardware-backed keys (if available), and a signed node registry we can validate in the control plane.

I attached a lightweight checklist and a first-pass playbook for node onboarding. Can you confirm: do you have a HSM or KMS on-site? Also, what's your preferred tooling for host provisioning (PXE + Ansible, or metal-as-a-service)?

If that looks good, we can iterate on exact disk sizes for the NVMe / blockstore split and produce a sample BOM.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: nephro-k8s-onprem-checklist.pdf (9KB), node-credentialing-playbook.md (3KB)

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers: we do have an on-site HSM (Thales) and we use pxeboot + terraform + ansible for provisioning. A few follow-ups from our infra team:

- For NVMe local scratch: can you call out expected per-node throughput/IOPS envelope so we can size controllers?
- For model store: we prefer a replicated blockstore across two racks; is async detach okay for fast failover?
- On credentialing: we need offline node rotation tooling and audit log hooks forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk).

If you can incorporate those constraints, we should be able to validate with our security team.

Thanks,
Alice
Head of Infrastructure, Nephro Systems

Diego / Laura / Alice —

Quick notes from the runtime team on NVMe sizing and detach semantics:

- We recommend reserving ~25% headroom on each worker NVMe for KV cache churn; for Nephro's profile IOPS target ~150k read IOPS and 30k write IOPS per NVMe device under peak. That typically maps to 2 x enterprise NVMe per node (1.6TB+) or 4 x smaller devices depending on budget.
- Async detach is acceptable provided the CNI/csi layer supports fast local reattachment and the model store is replicated at the volume layer (not just S3 style eventually-consistent object store).
- We'll surface a node affinity policy to prevent model-store-attached pods landing on nodes that are also doing heavy local scratch writes.

I'll add a short table to the checklist with recommended SKUs and rough cost delta.

- Aditya
Principal Infrastructure Engineer

Subject: Re: On-prem K8s blueprint: IO surface separation & node credentialing onboarding

Alice —

Thanks for the details. We've updated the checklist and playbook with:

- NVMe sizing guidance (Aditya's numbers) and two SKUs options (performance / cost).
- Blockstore deployment pattern: synchronous replication at controller layer across the two racks you mentioned; async detach preserved for node reclamation flows but we limit it to <30s to avoid long scheduling delays.
- Node onboarding flow: bootstrap via temporary token issued by your HSM-backed CA, node registers to a signed registry artifact, agent performs HSM-backed attestation, node receives short-lived certs that rotate every 24 hours by default.
- Audit forwarding: we added a Splunk forwarder container spec and log sink recommendations.

Next steps:
- Marissa will schedule a 60-minute workshop with your infra and security teams to walk through the playbook and collect any redlines.
- After that, we'll produce a BOM and a sample kubeadm/CSI config you can run in staging.

Marissa — can you propose times this week?

Diego
